h.strategy: Aim for hypotheses you believe are about 60-75% likely to hold but that a careful expert would call uncertain: conditional effects rather than main effects. Good sources are diminishing returns (an improving edit helps less when the parent already has a similar strong component), damage concentration (a harmful edit hurts more when the parent has few alternative routes or little spare capacity), and asymmetry (adding a capability and removing it need not have mirror-image effects). Each hypothesis should name the mechanism in one sentence. Avoid claims that are merely definitional or true by construction, and avoid claims that need an unusual sign reversal to be true.

hyps.why: Adding a missing direct input-output path helps far more than replacing an existing conv or pool with a skip.
Adding the first learned op on the final edge gives a larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
With edge 1 absent, edge 0 is the only way to feed nodes 1 and 2, so a strong conv there matters more.
Removing edge 4 hurts more when edge 3 is absent and fewer routes reach the output.
With edge 1 absent, edge 2 is the only way into node 2 from node 1, so a conv there carries more value.
With edge 1 gone, removing edge 0 cuts off nodes 1 and 2 and concentrates the damage.
Adding an intermediate connection helps more than swapping a stronger op for a 1x1 conv, which is likely negative.
A skip already provides a strong direct path, so the conv upgrade gains less than over none.
Pooling only helps by adding a path, so it helps more over none than when it replaces a conv.
A parallel strong conv into the output makes the added conv partly redundant, so its benefit shrinks.
